elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: Total external debt rose from 2015 to a peak before declining slightly through 2025. The printed 2025 value is 3,313, compared with 2,004 in 2015.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations
elements.description: The top stacked bar divides total external debt into public and publicly guaranteed, private nonguaranteed, and short-term debt; short-term debt is the largest component. The next bar divides public and publicly guaranteed debt among multilateral, bilateral, and private creditors, with private creditors largest. Lower bars detail multilateral and bilateral creditors: other multilateral is the largest multilateral item, while Japan is the largest bilateral item and China the smallest.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of East Asia and Pacific DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show external debt relative to exports and GNI and debt service relative to exports and GNI from 2015 to 2025. The printed 2025 ratios range from 55% for external debt / exports to 2% for debt service / GNI; all four show negative changes.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of East Asia and Pacific DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes compare average terms in 2025. The Official creditors box lists maturity of 24 years, a grace period of 7 years, and an interest rate of 3.2%; the Private creditors box lists 10 years, 6 years, and 4.1%, respectively. Official commitments have longer maturity and grace periods, while private commitments have the higher interest rate.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
